title: SeqLen-aware concurrency modeling for multi-GPU inference (throughput & p95 stability)
creator: Arjun Patel
description: Goal: Build a sequence-length aware concurrency model and measurement harness that predicts and validates multi-GPU throughput and p95 stability for TP/PP model deployments. Many production workloads have heavy seqlen variance (short chat turns vs. long documents). Current throughput tests assume fixed seqlen and steady concurrency which underestimates p95 regressions under bursty, mixed-length traffic. This ticket is to design, implement, and run a repeatable benchmark and a regression detector that accounts for seqlen distribution and KV-cache warmup effects.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable harness supports mixed seqlen distributions (custom histogram or sample traces)
Reports tokens/sec, median latency, p50/p95/p99 per seqlen bucket and aggregated, plus token-level tokenization-normalized throughput
Regression detector flags >10% p95 uplift relative to baseline with a false positive rate <5% on historical noise (validated on 30-day window)
Benchmark reproducibility: end-to-end run variance <7% for tokens/sec across 5 identical trials after warmup
Automated dashboard and alerting integration (Grafana panel + alert rule) with links to run artifacts
test_plan: 1) Implement harness extension to feed mixed-length sequences and control prefix KV warmup. 2) Run baseline matrix across target topologies: 2xA100 (tp1 pp2), 4xA100 (tp2 pp2), 8xA100 (tp4 pp2). 3) For each topology sweep: concurrency sweep (1..64), request inter-arrival jitter models (poisson, burst), and warmup patterns (cold, prefilled KV, incremental prefill). 4) Collect per-request latency, token counts, GPU utilization, queue depth, and KV hit rates. 5) Run regression detector offline against baseline and then in CI for future regressions.
benchmark_config: jitter models: poisson(λ), burst(windowed 200 reqs/s for 10s), steady
results_summary: Initial 3/02 run (4xA100, seqlen mix above, tp2 pp2): found expected drop in aggregate tokens/sec at high concurrency but an unexpected p95 cliff between concurrency 16->32 driven by queueing amplification for long-seq requests. KV prefill reduced p95 by ~18% at concurrency=32 but increased median latency for short seqs by 6% due to contention on prefill throughput. GPU utilization profiles showed head-of-line blocking where long requests delayed batch formation for short requests.
regression_detection: Design: sliding-window baseline aggregator (last N successful benchmark runs) per topology+seqlen-hist bucket. Compute p95 uplift = (current_p95 - baseline_p95)/baseline_p95. Use bootstrap sampling to estimate CI and require p95 uplift >10% with p < 0.01 to alert. Add an additional filter to ignore runs with throughput variance >15% (noisy runs). Detector implemented as a lightweight service + unit tests; integration planned with runtime-telemetry to pull GPU counters for correlation.
decisions: Use seqlen-bucketed aggregation rather than single global p95 to avoid masking long-tail effects
Implement KV prefill as an independent toggle in harness (do not conflate with model warmup)
Prefer bootstrap CI over parametric tests due to heavy-tailed latency distributions
Store run artifacts (profiles, flamegraphs, GPU counters) in S3 with run metadata for reproducibility
blockers: Intermittent host-level NIC saturation observed at high burst rates on our 4xA100 racks — infra ticket raised with Ops (INC-2026-14). Until resolved, top-end concurrency runs may show network-induced artifacts.
